what: Khardah, with Santipur and Saidabad, one of three centres of Chaitanya Vaishnavism; Gosains of Khardah descend from Nityananda; quoted from Risley. Vaishnava Gosains, NOT Daśanāmī.
quote: Khardah, between Calcutta and Barrnokpore, the home of the Gosains, or religious mendicants who traced their descent from Nityananda, a devoted disciple of Chaitanya

what: Vaishnava Gosains are Brahmans, hereditary gurus; organised in circles with adhikari, faujdar, chharidar; prosperous traders and money-lenders; marry Srotriya and Bansaja Brahmans. Vaishnava, not Daśanāmī.
quote: Most of them aro prosperous traders and money-lendere, onriched by the gifts of the laity and by the ivheritanve of all property left by Buitagis.

what: Vaishnava Gosains are described as traders and money-lenders enriched by inheriting property of deceased Bairagis (Vaishnava, not Daśanāmī).
quote: Most of them aro prosperous traders and money-lendere, onriched by the gifts of the laity and by the ivheritanve of all property left by Buitagis.

what: Khardah a great Vaishnava pilgrimage place; fairs at Dol and Ras festivals; temple of Shyamsunder.
quote: Khardah has become a great place of pilgrimage for the seot, and large numbers flock thither on the occasion of the fairs held at the Dol and Ras festivals

what: Nityananda settled at Khardah living the life of an ascetic; his son Birbhadra founded the line of Goswamis of Khardah, gurus of the Vaishnavas.
quote: From Nitydnanda's son Birbhadra are descended the Goswamis or Gosains of Khardah, who are regarded as gurus, or spiritual guides, by the Vaishnavas.

what: Makara Sankranti bathing fair at Sagar Island, temple of Kapilmuni; no Sannyasi or Bairagi is mentioned in the Gazetteer account (priests keep the image and share pilgrims' gifts).
quote: the point of junction of the river and sea at Sagar Island is a celebrated seat of Hindu pilgrimage, to which thousands of devout pilgrims repair every year during the great bathing festival.

what: Muhammadan fakirs act as tiger-charmers for wood-cutters (descendants of Mobrah Ghazi); Muslim, not Daśanāmī; for comparison only.
